newsitem.title: CANADA: Wal-Mart Canada launches Internet shopping.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart Canada launches Internet shopping.

text.p: Wal-Mart Canada Inc, a unit of Wal-Mart Stores Inc, is testing a program that enables shoppers in remote areas of Canada to order merchandise over the Internet, the company said on Thursday.
Launched today, the online "cyber shopper" program makes merchandise available to communities located more than 125 km from a Wal-Mart store.

Under the program, customers can review merchandise, including clothing, household and seasonal items, from a Wal-Mart cyber flyer in English and French. Orders will be delivered C.O.D. to remote communities by regular Canada Post service.
The cyber shopper test program will run until early autumn and be evaluated based on customer response.
Analysts said the Wal-Mart move was unlikely to hurt Sears Canada Inc, which operates a catologue shopping system across Canada.
"Sears (has) an established base," said First Marathon Securities retail analyst Perry Caicco, who said the new Wal-Mart service was of "more PR (public relations) value than anything else."
